family: Hierarchical traversal and confidence-gated broad-to-fine classification
source: Hierarchical decisions row of the build-spec pattern table
description: One compact three-level intake taxonomy (7 divisions plus an explicit other option, 5 groups per division, 4 categories per group) is reused by every case, so per-node accuracy aggregates across the suite. Each level is its own Choice question; deeper questions name the gold parent path in their instructions, so a level is scored conditioned on a correct parent (teacher forced). Every question is prefilled independently, so a deeper question never leaks its parent into a shallower one. Cases are built around near-miss sibling pairs at each depth, which makes two metrics available from one run: per-node accuracy and full-path exact match, and the gap between them is the finding. Three case shapes go beyond plain traversal. Beam frontier cases batch one group Choice for the gold division and one for a rival division whose gold answer is none_applicable, which is the pruning signal. Broad-to-fine pairs give both twins an identical group option set that includes insufficient_detail, so the determined and underdetermined members of a pair differ only in the state and their Choice confidences can be compared directly. Rerank cases score one Noul per candidate division and rank them by P(true). Metrics this suite supports: level-1 accuracy, full-path exact match, backoff-adjusted accuracy that credits the division when the group is wrong, and the paired confidence separation between each bf-x-determined case and its bf-x-underdetermined twin. It does not measure flat intent classification (covered by the BANKING77 set), calibration in any absolute sense (the conditional softmax is uncalibrated, which is why the confidence test is a within-pair comparison and not a threshold), or multi-request beam search executed end to end, since the caller joins levels itself.

cases.name: nightly-load-field-rename
cases.rationale: The feed arrived and rows were written, so this is not an ingestion failure; the stated cause is the vendor renaming and retyping a field.

request.state: Nightly load report for the partner-claims feed, run 2026-03-11. The run finished in 41 minutes, which is inside the usual window, and the operator on duty signed it off before the downstream alert fired at 06:20. The source file landed on time at 01:05 and all 214,880 rows were read. Of those rows, 214,612 were written to the staging table with a null member key, because the vendor's release notes for version 9 renamed member_id to memberId and changed it from an integer to a zero-padded string; our loader still looks for the old name and type and silently defaults the column. The remaining rows came from a legacy path that still sends the old field. No file was missing, nothing was loaded twice, and no one has asked us to reprocess an earlier window. Downstream eligibility checks now show a sharp drop in matched members, which is the symptom that raised this ticket.
